# PR #4103: Patch (part 10 of 20): the publicly cached API responses are the same for every caller, with a test (cache poisoning)

Closes #4011

## What changed

Cache-poisoning guards for the six public routes answered through `cached_ok` (`crates/server/src/api/stats.rs`), which marks bodies `public, max-age=…` for shared caches keyed on the URL alone:

- `crates/server/src/api/stats.rs`: doc comment on `cached_ok` stating the no-caller rule — only `AuthLevel::None` routes whose handlers never read the caller may use it (no `req.caller`, `caller_of`/`caller_profile`, `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Accept-Language`, `X-Forwarded-*`, `X-Original-URL`/`X-Rewrite-URL`, or any other caller-carried header; unknown query params stay ignored). Signature unchanged.
- `crates/server/tests/api/stats.rs`: new `mod cache_poisoning` with a `get_with` helper, a `seven_ways` helper (bare, signed in, `Accept-Language`, `Cookie`, four forged forward/rewrite headers, unknown `?poison=1` query param, all at once), and five tests asserting 200 + `public, max-age=<route TTL>` + byte-identical serialized bodies across all seven variants, for `/api/stats/cards`, `/api/stats/cards/core-001`, `/api/stats/play-rates`, `/api/stats/games`, and `/api/stats/players`.
- `crates/server/tests/api/ci_runs.rs`: new `mod cache_poisoning` with one test of the same shape for `GET /api/stats/ci` against canned GitHub data (a passed run, so no jobs are read).
- `apps/edge/src/config.test.ts`: new `#4011 nothing in front caches /api/*` block — `wrangler.jsonc` and `infra/cloudflare.tf` contain no `cache`, the Worker sources never touch the Cache API (`caches`, `cacheTtl`, `cacheEverything`), and `public/_headers` has no `/api` rule.

Caller-blindness was verified, not assumed: all six routes declare `AuthLevel::None` in `app.rs`, `dispatch` (`http.rs`) resolves a caller only when `auth != AuthLevel::None`, and the only caller reads in either file are `get_player`/`put_player`, which answer through `ok_of`, never `cached_ok`. `infra/cloudflare.tf` was read only, not changed.

## How it was tested

- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server cache_poisoning` — 6 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::stats::` — 55 passed; `api::ci_runs::` — 5 passed (full files, covering the touched area).
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean; `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `pnpm --dir apps/edge test src/config.test.ts` — 23 passed (19 existing + 4 new).
- `cargo run --release -p jackioh-tools -- spec check` — ok (2231 rulings, 5664 proofs).

## Decisions

- Serialized-`Value` equality stands in for wire bytes, since `cached_ok` sends `body.to_string()` of a deterministically serialized `Value`; rejected byte-capture via the response body because `read_json` already parses it and re-serialization is exact here.
- Header insertion uses `headers_mut().insert` with `parse::<HeaderName>()` (replacing `json_request`'s default `X-Forwarded-For` for the spoof variant); rejected passing `&&str` straight to `insert` after the compiler's E0283 inference error.
- Sensitivity follows the plan's accepted argument: the seven variants provably differ on the wire by construction, and grep proves no handler reads caller state; a kept server-side cell could mask a *future* header read, which is why the doc comment bars adding one (the issue's stated residual risk).
- One caveat: a full `api::` suite run was launched and finished, but its terminal output never reached this session, so it is not claimed — the two touched files' full runs above are the regression evidence.

## Reviewer notes

- The `/cache/i` tripwires on `wrangler.jsonc` and `cloudflare.tf` are deliberately broad: any future key containing "cache" must consciously reaffirm `/api/*` stays uncached.
- `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9` overrides the test default IP, exercising a different rate-limit bucket; `AuthLevel::None` routes skip the address budget check anyway, and each test uses a fresh `test_app()`.

### Its own review

# #4011: Patch (part 10 of 20): the publicly cached API responses are the same for every caller, with a test (cache poisoning)
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

### What it does

Item 10 of #3897: **cache poisoning**. A cache keyed on the URL stores a response shaped by a header it didn't key on, and serves it to everyone. First-pass verdict: 🔍 to check.

Every API response is `no-store` except those sent through `cached_ok` (`crates/server/src/api/stats.rs`), which says `public, max-age=…`. These are its six callers:

- `api/stats.rs`, lines 1322, 1354, 1450, 1520 and 1636;
- `api/ci_runs.rs`, line 309.

1. **A test per route.** The same path and query must give a byte-identical body whatever else the request carries:
   - signed in or not (`Authorization`);
   - `Accept-Language`;
   - `Cookie`;
   - `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Original-URL` and `X-Rewrite-URL`;
   - an unknown query parameter.
2. **No caller in any of them.** None of these routes reads the caller, so a later change can't make one personal while it stays public. Say so in `cached_ok`'s doc comment.
3. **Nothing caches `/api/*` in front.** No Cloudflare Cache Rule caches `/api/*` (`infra/cloudflare.tf` has none today), and the Worker (`apps/edge/src`) never calls the Cache API for it. If there is a config test that fits, add the check there.

### Acceptance

- The per-route tests pass, and `cached_ok`'s comment states the rule.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server` and the whole-workspace gates green.

### Blocked by, part of

Part of #3897.

### Difficulty (a guess)

medium: anything that is not hard

### Who does it

The night bot (bot:build)

6. In `apps/edge/src/config.test.ts`, add `describe("#4011 nothing in front caches /api/*", …)` following the file's existing `readFileSync(join(ROOT, …))` pattern: (a) raw `wrangler.jsonc` text does not match `/cache/i`; (b) `infra/cloudflare.tf` text does not match `/cache/i` (today it has no cache-rule, page-rule or ruleset resource at all); (c) `apps/edge/src/index.ts` plus `routing.ts` text does not match `/\bcaches\b/` nor `/cacheTtl|cacheEverything/i` (the Worker never calls the Cache API; its only `Cache-Control` write is the wasm module's in `precompressedModule`); (d) `apps/web/public/_headers` text does not match `/^\/api/m` (its only cache blocks are `/*`, `/fonts/*`, `/assets/*`).

Confirm each new test fails without its guard (e.g. temporarily reading a header into the body is not required — instead verify sensitivity by dropping one variant's assertion mentally; the honest check is that all 7 variants actually differ in what they send, which the helper guarantees).

## Tests

- `crates/server/tests/api/stats.rs`, `mod cache_poisoning`: the five `cache_poisoning_*_same_bytes_whatever_the_caller_carries` tests above; each asserts 200 + `public, max-age=<TTL>` + one identical serialized body across 7 header/query variants. Command: `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::stats::cache_poisoning`.
- `crates/server/tests/api/ci_runs.rs`, `mod cache_poisoning`: `cache_poisoning_ci_runs_same_bytes_whatever_the_caller_carries`, same shape against canned GitHub data. Command: `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::ci_runs::cache_poisoning`.
- `apps/edge/src/config.test.ts`, `#4011` describe: four static assertions over `wrangler.jsonc`, `infra/cloudflare.tf`, the Worker's sources, and `_headers`. Command: `pnpm --dir apps/edge test src/config.test.ts`.

## Done when

- [ ] All six cached routes have a per-route byte-identical-body test covering signed-in, `Accept-Language`, `Cookie`, the four forward/rewrite headers, and an unknown query param, and each passes.
- [ ] `cached_ok`'s doc comment states the no-caller rule.
- [ ] The edge config test pins no `/api/*` caching in front (tf, wrangler, Worker source, `_headers`) and passes.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, both server test filters, the edge file test, and `cargo jackioh spec check` are green.

## Risks

- Kept server-side cells (`kept_window`, play-rates/CI kept answers) mean a repeat request can pass even if a future handler reads a header after the cache lookup; the tests still catch any header-dependent body built per request, which is the poisoning vector that matters, and the doc comment bars adding such reads.
- Varying `X-Forwarded-For` changes the rate-limit address hash, not the body; a fresh `test_app()` per test plus 7 sequential requests stays far under the limiter, but keep one app per test, not one shared across tests.
- `serde_json::to_string` equality stands in for wire bytes; it is exact here because `cached_ok` sends `body.to_string()` of a deterministically-serialized `Value`.
- The `/cache/i` tripwires on config files will fire on any future legitimate key containing "cache"; that is deliberate — the builder of that change must then consciously reaffirm `/api/*` stays uncached.

## Open questions

- None. Every check the task asks for fits a file the bot may change; `infra/cloudflare.tf` needs reading only, since it already contains no cache rules.
